precepts.text: She goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, and meeteth them in every thought. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought: what is the outcome of this thought? In an argument with your husband, the thought says say this word and you can trigger him; filter it for godly intentions. 2 Corinthians 13:10: the power the Lord gave is to edification, and not to destruction. Someone's positive word may land negative because Satan knows what you are going through and uses their vessel; you choose to respond for edification or to bring contention, or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.

precepts.text: All the gods of the nations are idols. Name a kingdom that kept God's commandments; they fall because they serve idols, and Babylon the Great holds all the idols of every kingdom.
precepts.point: The desire of wisdom bringeth to a kingdom; if your delight be in thrones and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, honour wisdom that ye may reign for evermore. The only way Israel's kingdom lasts for ever is wisdom and humility toward God.
precepts.why:
Wisdom tells the kings of the earth that “the desire of wisdom bringeth to a kingdom”, and to “honour wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore.” David shows why the kingdoms of the nations never did: “For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols”.

They are all idols. All kingdoms fall because they do not walk after the wisdom of God. Name a kingdom that has kept the commandments of God. They don't. They fall because they serve idol gods, and pride destroys them, as it destroyed Herod, who gave not God the glory and was eaten of worms. Assyrian, Babylon, Greek, Rome, America: nobody is exempt from pride and God destroying them.

It is no different with Babylon the Great. This Edomite has the most gods of all: he has all the idol gods of every kingdom wrapped up in one, in different forms. That is why Obadiah follows, “concerning Edom”, the white man, the Caucasian, his biblical name: “thou art greatly despised”, and “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. None of the kings before him, Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Greeks or Romans, was more prideful than Esau.

The same judgment is on us. The power God gave was given to us by God too, and for our pride as a nation we have been destroyed. The only way our kingdom will last for ever is when we walk in wisdom and humility toward God. Outside of that, the kingdom comes down, the same as it did with all the nations before us.

precepts.text: Consuming envy has no fellowship with wisdom; the brothers' envy put wisdom away from them.
precepts.point: His brethren envied him, but his father observed the saying. Envy consumes a man, and such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom; when envy takes over, wisdom leaves.
precepts.why:
“Neither will I go with consuming envy; for such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom.” Envy is consuming: it eats a man up. And a man consumed by it has no fellowship with wisdom; when envy takes over, wisdom leaves.

That is what happened to Joseph’s brethren. “And his brethren envied him”: their envy put wisdom away from them, and with wisdom gone there was nothing to hold back what they went on to do to their brother. Their father, on the other hand, “observed the saying.”

precepts.text: The word to them that hold thrones is addressed to kings; the sceptre speaks of a king.
precepts.point: There shall come a Star out of Jacob: the Star is Christ, the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: the sceptre belongs to kings, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel.” To whom does the sceptre belong? Wisdom's word on thrones and sceptres is addressed to kings: “Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth. Give ear, ye that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations.”

The sceptre speaks of a king, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

precepts.text: Thrones and sceptres belong to kings; the Sceptre rising out of Israel is Christ the King.
precepts.point: There shall come a Star out of Jacob: the Star is Christ, the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: the sceptre belongs to kings, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“If your delight be then in thrones and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, honour wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore.” Thrones and sceptres belong to kings.

So “a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel” is the King rising out of Israel: Christ the King, the same Star out of Jacob.

precepts.text: Hear, O ye kings, and understand; for power is given you of the Lord and sovereignty from the highest, who shall try your works and search out your counsels; rulers hold a small power from the Most High until the King comes.
precepts.point: He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God, and he shall be as the light of the morning when the sun riseth, a morning without clouds, as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain. This is how you are a great leader: just in your judgments, in the fear of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

precepts.why:
“Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth. Give ear, ye that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations. For power is given you of the Lord, and sovereignty from the Highest, who shall try your works, and search out your counsels.”

In his last words David says, “The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.” Rulers hold a small power from the Most High until the King comes, and the Highest will try their works and search out their counsels. So the one who rules must be just in his judgments, in the fear of the Most High. This is how you are a great leader.

And such a ruler “shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.”

David could say this because “The Spirit of the Lord spake by me, and his word was in my tongue.” David was a prophet, the sweet psalmist of Israel, and the book of Psalms are songs of prophecy.

precepts.text: Wisdom is plain and easily seen by those that love and seek her.
precepts.point: Like Christ saying he that has ears let him hear, everyone has ears, but only the one with understanding truly hears the wisdom coming out.

note.label: Proverbs 8: Wisdom Crieth in the Streets and Christ Set Up from Everlasting

precepts.why:
“They are all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.” Wisdom's words are plain, but plain to a certain one: him that understands and them that find knowledge. Like Christ saying he that has ears let him hear, everyone has ears, but only the one with understanding truly hears the wisdom coming out.

Wisdom of Solomon says the same: “Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yea, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.” She is easily seen, but of them that love her; found, but of such as seek her. Wisdom is plain to those that love and seek her.

So wisdom is not hidden; the difference is in the one hearing. Her words are excellent and right, all in righteousness, and to the one who loves and seeks her they are easily seen.
